summary: Sound and shape-disjoint. It reuses the parent's stream-K A8/B8 for sliding verify, where all three shapes are latency-bound (1-4 tiles per CTA) and the FA3 path pays for 5 launches. Dispatch only after full-verify-cuda-streamk-splitkv passes its self-check and the 16 tests. Fix the edge-mask predicate and the build/self-check coupling below. The verify_1 target (9-11 us) is optimistic; ~12 us is more likely, which is still a clear gain.
justification: The mechanism is plausible. FINDINGS gives the incumbent sliding verify shapes as 17.6 / 22.8 / 29.3 us against floors of 0.1 / 1.9 / 3.7 us. They are pure latency plus launch count: FA3 main is 7.4 / 10.7 / 14.7 us, and prepare_varlen (1.8-1.9), FlashAttnFwdCombine (3.8-4.2) and rms_norm_gate (1.1-1.5) together are ~7 us of serial small kernels plus graph-node gaps. Replacing FA3 main + prepare + combine + norm-gate with A8 + B8 (norm-gate fused into B8, no prepare) removes two launches and the separate combine/norm pass. The windowed range is right. lo_b = max(0, seq_b - 8 - (window - 1)) gives 2055 keys = 33 tiles at ctx 80K, and the mask t >= seq_b - 8 + j - (window - 1) is exactly FA3 window_size=(window-1, 0) as master passes it, so every key of each query's 2048-key window is attended. The expected directions match TASK. Sliding is ~62% / 29% / 22% of the verify_1/16/32 load times (46 x 17.6 vs 16 x 30.3, and so on), and decode and full shapes are outside the gate. Weakest link: the verify_1 estimate (A8 ~3-4 us, B8 ~2 us). The incumbent FA3 main already runs the same dependent chain (cache_seqlens -> page index -> K/V gather -> mma) over 33-ish splits in 7.4 us. A8 at one tile per CTA runs that same chain from a cold L2, with three dependent DRAM round trips plus the q-block fetch, so it is unlikely to be much under ~4-5 us. B8 has its own chain (seqlens -> partials -> gate). The landed fused Triton sliding kernel, one launch at decode_1, takes 10.3 us. Realistically verify_1 lands at ~11-13 us, not 9-11: ~1.35-1.6x on the shape and ~1.2-1.3x on the verify_1 load, still a clear signal well outside the CI. verify_16 (2 tiles per CTA) and verify_32 (4 per CTA, ~17 MB) should be 13-17 and 17-21 us. The math is trivial here, so the parent's MUFU and shared-memory ceilings do not bind. Design notes: (a) The spec applies the per-row mask only on the request's first and last tiles. That is correct at ctx 80K, because (seq_b - lo_b) = 2055 and 2055 % 64 = 7, so the 7-key causal band sits exactly in the last tile. It is wrong whenever (seq_b - lo_b) % 64 is in 1..6, which happens for short requests with lo_b = 0: the causal band [seq_b-7, seq_b-1] then straddles the last two tiles. Use 'tile overlaps [lo_b, lo_b+7) or [seq_b-7, seq_b)' as the mask predicate, or just mask every tile on the sliding route (33 tiles, negligible ALU). The same straddle exists in the parent's full path when cache_seqlens % 64 is in 1..7. (b) The grid can be config-only min(2 x SM, B x ceil((window + 7) / 64)), which gives 33 at batch 1 instead of 264 with 231 empty CTAs. It is legal (shape-derived) and slightly cuts launch and drain. (c) Make window a template parameter (or a constexpr instantiation), so the full-verify window = 0 SASS is byte-identical to stage 2 and the 'full flat' expectation holds by construction.
confounders: full-verify-cuda-streamk-splitkv (parent, running, not landed): this run carries the parent's full verify_16/32 change too, so the headline mixes both. Attribute only on the sliding verify rows and top_kernels. If the parent ends up not promoted, the headline is not a measure of this change. If the parent's A8 has spills or is smem-bound, that matters little here, because sliding works on 1-4 tiles per CTA (latency, not throughput).

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv (landed, same load_inline module): adding the windowed instantiation to the shared module means a build failure or a shared self-check failure sets _EXT=None. That silently reverts full decode_16/32 (and the parent's verify) to FA3. It would show as regressions this change did not cause, and the sliding rows would read flat. Read the log tail ('[splitkv] load_inline failed' / 'SELF-CHECK FAILED') before attributing anything, and give the sliding route its own self-check flag.

fused-preattention-triton (landed): runs unchanged on both sides with ROPE on and PAIRED=False and stores the 8 new K/V rows that A8 reads in stream order. Its time (1.6/2.7/4.2 us) is common to incumbent and new, so there is no confound beyond requiring that A8 not be reordered before it.

sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate (landed): its early return is q_len == 1 only, so it is disjoint from the sliding verify route. No interaction, except that the new sliding-verify predicate must sit after that early return and not catch q_len 1.
interference: No companion is warranted. The gate is config-only and shape-disjoint: only sliding q_len 8, tp8, page 1 shapes change relative to the parent, and the pre-attention kernel is unchanged there (sliding was never paired). So the three sliding verify rows and their top_kernels (A8 + B8 vs FA3 main + prepare + combine + rms_norm_gate) attribute the effect directly. A gain or loss there cannot come from a landed hypothesis acting differently. An ab-revert of fused-preattention-triton would only change a cost common to both sides. A control splitting 'fewer launches' from 'A8 itself' (for example FA3 main + B8-style fused combine) is not implementable without FA3 internals and would not change the decision. The one interpretive hazard is the shared-module build and self-check coupling and the parent's headline contribution. Both are a log check and a per-shape reading, not an extra run.
rules_flags: None blocking. Grid and workspace come from the device and config only (keep any grid cap shape-derived, never from cache_seqlens values). There is no host sync, nothing is cached across calls, q is FP8 E4M3 (allowed), P@V is f16 (finer than FA3), and the KV cache stays FP8.

Every key: the window must be exactly window keys per query (window-1 back plus self). The lower-edge mask must not drop a valid key. Verify with a synthetic case where seq_b is in [window, window+7], so lo_b = 0 while the per-token lower bound is still positive.
The per-call torch.empty workspace is fine under graph capture (graph pool), as in stage 1.
open_questions: Dispatch ordering: run only after the parent harvests with M1 (all 16 tests pass and its self-check is OK in the log). If the parent's verify path fails, fix it first, because the sliding route shares A8/B8.

Self-check coverage: include batch 1 (the verify_1 target). Include lens with (seq_b - lo_b) % 64 in 1..6 (short lo_b = 0 requests, to catch the causal band straddling two tiles), seq_b in [window, window+7], seq_b < 8 + window, and full 2055-key windows. Use kv_scale 1 and 0.25 and several grids (3, 7, device), so that segments start and end mid-request and at the window lower edge.
Share one device helper for lo_b / tiles_b / TP between A8 and B8 (the window formula must match bit for bit), and keep the c_lo..c_hi inverse exact as the parent reviewer asked.

Merge hygiene with full-verify1-cuda-streamk-batch1 (also stacked on the parent; it widens _splitkv_verify_gate and sets grid = SM count at batch 1): put the sliding route in its own predicate (e.g. _splitkv_sliding_verify_gate) and key any batch-1 grid choice on window, so a later merge does not silently change sliding verify_1's grid.

Report from the profile: A8 and B8 times per sliding verify shape, and the shape time minus kernel sum (graph-node gaps). If A8 at verify_1 is > 5 us, the next lever is fusing pre-attention into A8's prologue for the sliding route (the queued fused-sliding-preattn-into-window-kernel idea, now on CUDA).
